title: Sell Mineral Rights in Leith-Hatfield, PA
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Leith-Hatfield, PA
metaDescription: Leith-Hatfield sits in Fayette County where coal and coke history overlaps wet-gas Marcellus acreage. Learn what that layered history means for your rights.
heroLead: Leith-Hatfield sits in Fayette County, where the coal and coke industry that built this part of Pennsylvania left behind mineral deeds that still shape what families own today.
intro: Fayette County's history is coke-oven history first — this was the heart of the Connellsville coke region, and the coal companies that ran those operations bought and reserved mineral rights aggressively across the county in the late 1800s and early 1900s. Leith-Hatfield sits right in that legacy, which means a lot of local mineral title runs back through old coal company chains before it ever gets to the modern Marcellus wet-gas question.

sections.heading: Coal, Coke, and Gas Are Often Separate Reservations
paragraphs: Old Fayette County deeds frequently reserved coal specifically, sometimes alongside oil and gas, sometimes not. We read each deed individually because the language varies significantly even between neighboring Leith-Hatfield parcels, depending on which coal company originally acquired the reservation and when.

Coke ovens once lined the hillsides not far from Leith-Hatfield, and the companies that ran them recorded some of the more complex mineral reservations we come across in this part of the state, which is exactly why we start every file with the original deed instead of a summary.

sections.heading: Fayette's Position on the Wet-Gas Edge
paragraphs: Southern Fayette County sits toward the edge of the Marcellus wet-gas window rather than its most productive center, which affects how aggressively operators have pursued leasing here compared to counties like Washington or Greene, but it hasn't stopped activity entirely.

sections.heading: What We Verify First
paragraphs: Before discussing a number, we confirm whether your Leith-Hatfield deed reserved coal, oil and gas, or both, whether any of those reservations have since been leased, and what current unit or drilling activity, if any, touches the parcel.

faqs.question: Does an old coal reservation mean we lost our gas rights too?
faqs.answer: Not necessarily — coal and oil/gas were frequently reserved as separate estates, so a coal-only reservation may leave gas rights with the surface owner or a different chain entirely.

faqs.question: Is Fayette County actively drilled for Marcellus gas?
faqs.answer: Less intensively than the core wet-gas counties to the north, but activity does extend into southern Fayette, and we check current status for specific parcels.

faqs.question: How far back do Leith-Hatfield mineral records typically go?
faqs.answer: Often to the late 1800s or early 1900s coal-boom era, which is why a careful deed read matters more here than in more recently developed areas.

faqs.question: How do you tell if a coal reservation from the 1900s also covered gas?
faqs.answer: We read the exact wording of the original severance deed — some Fayette County reservations used broad mineral language covering everything, others named coal specifically and left gas alone.
